params.body:
Fixes bevinding een-overkoop-kon-de-tijdslimiet-niet-halen, and closes bevinding een-overkoop-liet-geen-spoor-na (its unexplained 26 September case).

## What happened

`Vehicle::buy_over` copied every platform photo (two `Storage::copy` calls on the bucket per photo), then every damage with its photos, then the options, and only after that wrote the `vehicle_history` row, rang the bell and sent the two mails. Production kills a request after 30 seconds (php-fpm `request_terminate_timeout`, `max_execution_time` and nginx `fastcgi_read_timeout` are all 30), and a killed process logs nothing.

On 26 September vehicle 23098 (19 platform photos, 18 damages, 98 options) was bought over as 23114. The copy got photos 1 to 11, no damages, no options, no history row and no mails; `23114/stocklist_car_image_11.jpeg` is in the bucket and its thumbnail is not, so the request died between the two copies of the eleventh photo. A comparable purchase (22916, also 19 photos) finished in time: it is a race against the bucket. #842 was a different cause with the same symptom.

## The change

- **The sale first.** In the request: guard, original sold, copy created, options copied (plain rows), history row, bell, both mails, each in its own try as before. Then `CopyBoughtVehicleMedia` is dispatched, also in its own try.
- **`App\Jobs\CopyBoughtVehicleMedia`** copies the platform photos, the damages and their photos. It is on the `default` queue: the production worker is documented as `queue:work --queue=default,webhook` (CUTOVER.md section 4), and `BuildShowroomZip` and the photo jobs (`ProcessImage`) already rely on that queue. `tries = 3`, `timeout = 300` (under the worker's 328 s and the queue's `retry_after` of 400 s), backoff 30/120 s. A file that exists at the source but did not arrive makes the run throw, so the worker retries.
- **`App\Support\BoughtVehicleCopy`** completes rather than copies, so every run is safe to repeat: a photo matches on its file name, a damage on location and note, a damage photo on its file name, an option on `option_id` (`vehicle_option_unique` allows one row per option per car). A file is only copied when the copy's file is missing. Rows the buyer deleted on the copy (withTrashed) are not brought back. The `?string` "copy or ignore" semantics from #842 are kept.
- **Damage photos go under the copy's folder** (`{copy id}/{file name}`, with the copy's `vehicle_id`), as `ImageController::upload_damage` stores them. The old code wrote them under `{new damage id}/...`, a folder that can also belong to the car with that id, and left `vehicle_id` on the original, so deleting the original (`VehicleObserver::deleted`) removed the copy's damage photo rows.
- **Order path.** `OrderController::store` and `createFromOffer` call the same helper and benefit the same way. Nothing there reads the copy's photos: the order is created from ids, and both mail views (`mails/sold_email`, `mails/bought_email`) show the photo of the ORIGINAL (`$existing_vehicle->primary_photo`). Until the job has run (seconds, with a worker) the copy's sheet shows no platform photos or damages.
- **Outside production** the queue is `sync` (`Outbound::seal`), so the job runs inside the request there, but after the sale is written; a failing copy is reported and the purchase stands.

## The repair: `stocklist:complete-buy-over {copy} {--apply}`

Runs the same code synchronously on a copy that was cut off: missing photos (including a missing thumbnail, only when the target file is missing), damages with their photos, and options. Dry run by default; `--apply` writes. It never writes a `vehicle_history` row and never sends mail. Not run on production.

## Rules

New rule R S5-3.16 (a buy-over does not wait for the photos). New finding `2026-09-29-een-overkoop-kon-de-tijdslimiet-niet-halen.md`; `2026-09-28-een-overkoop-liet-geen-spoor-na.md` gets a section explaining the 26 September case and is set to opgelost.

## Tests

`ABuyOverDoesNotWaitForThePhotosTest` (7 tests): the history row, both mails and the options exist with the queue faked and no photo copied yet, and the job is pushed on `default`; a bucket that refuses every copy does not take the sale with it; the job brings photos (own photos excluded), damage and damage photo over; a copy cut off halfway is completed by two job runs without duplicates, including the missing thumbnail; a photo the buyer deleted stays deleted; the command's dry run writes nothing, `--apply` completes, a second `--apply` adds nothing, and no history row or mail comes from it; a car that is not a copy is refused. The first and third fail against the old helper. Full suite locally: 2296 tests; the one failure was an unresolvable source reference in the new rule, fixed, and the rules and buy-over tests rerun green.
params.title: A sale does not wait for the photos
